agent.role: Read-only API designer. Verify the current source and tests, and design the smallest additive request-ref-correlated stream delivery API. Do not edit, commit, or run network commands. Address queued requests, early deltas, completion ordering, cancellation, callback compatibility, recipient death, and deterministic tests. Separate core scope from Ensemble follow-up. prompt:
Found in a read-only review of `main` at `b8f8ab4`. Code links point at that commit; `main` has moved since (core 0.4.0).

## Problem

`c:handle_stream_event/2` ([`lib/gen_agent.ex:277`](https://github.com/genagent/gen_agent/blob/b8f8ab4/lib/gen_agent.ex#L277)) and `c:pre_turn/2` ([`lib/gen_agent.ex:328`](https://github.com/genagent/gen_agent/blob/b8f8ab4/lib/gen_agent.ex#L328)) do not receive the request ref, and `run_prompt/7` ([`lib/gen_agent/server.ex:785-795`](https://github.com/genagent/gen_agent/blob/b8f8ab4/lib/gen_agent/server.ex#L785-L795), 811-838) runs the prompt task without it, so callback code has no in-band way to tag a stream event with the ref returned by `tell/3` or `tell_with_completion/4`. `tell_with_completion/4` sends one terminal message (server.ex:1267-1271, 1286-1290) and no telemetry event is emitted per stream event (server.ex:1332-1394). An application that renders deltas must add forwarding to each agent module, as gen_agent_live/lib/gen_agent_live/chat_agent.ex:68-93 and fio/lib/fio/capo.ex:68-77 do. Correlation is possible only indirectly: turns are serialized, and `[:gen_agent, :prompt, :start]` carries the ref, but that event is emitted after the task is spawned (server.ex:784-797), so its ordering relative to the first delta is not guaranteed. Fix options: an opt-in `stream_to` recipient on `tell_with_completion` producing `{:gen_agent, :event, name, ref, event}`, an optional `handle_stream_event/3` with the ref, or a `[:gen_agent, :stream, :event]` telemetry event carrying `agent` and `ref` in line with the README's telemetry-first principle ([`README.md:191-195`](https://github.com/genagent/gen_agent/blob/b8f8ab4/README.md#L191-L195)).

**Evidence.** [`lib/gen_agent.ex:277`](https://github.com/genagent/gen_agent/blob/b8f8ab4/lib/gen_agent.ex#L277) `@callback handle_stream_event(Event.t(), agent_state()) :: agent_state()`; [`lib/gen_agent.ex:328`](https://github.com/genagent/gen_agent/blob/b8f8ab4/lib/gen_agent.ex#L328) `@callback pre_turn(prompt :: String.t(), agent_state()) :: pre_turn_return()`. [`lib/gen_agent/server.ex:935-941`](https://github.com/genagent/gen_agent/blob/b8f8ab4/lib/gen_agent/server.ex#L935-L941) invokes `module.handle_stream_event(event, state)` inside the prompt task with no ref in scope (the ref is not passed to `run_prompt/7`, [`lib/gen_agent/server.ex:784-795`](https://github.com/genagent/gen_agent/blob/b8f8ab4/lib/gen_agent/server.ex#L784-L795)). The ref is available only in `[:gen_agent, :prompt, :start]` telemetry and in `handle_response/3` after the turn. [`lib/gen_agent/server.ex:1267-1271`](https://github.com/genagent/gen_agent/blob/b8f8ab4/lib/gen_agent/server.ex#L1267-L1271) sends a single completion message per request. No guide under guides/patterns uses `handle_stream_event`.

**Scenario.** A LiveView chat sends `tell_with_completion` and wants to render text deltas for that message. The agent module must be written to broadcast from `handle_stream_event/2` to a topic stored in its state, and the LiveView cannot tell which request a delta belongs to when prompts are queued.

## Proposed fix

- Add an opt-in stream recipient to `tell_with_completion` (for example `stream_to: pid` producing `{:gen_agent, :event, name, ref, event}` messages sent from the prompt task), or add an optional `handle_stream_event/3` that receives the request ref.

## Acceptance

- The new behaviour is covered by tests and documented in the relevant moduledoc.

## Verification

- Confirmed by an independent code trace.
- Reported independently by 2 other review passes.



Design a concrete implementation for current main. In particular choose whether stream_to on tell_with_completion, a callback arity, or telemetry is the safest first slice, and explain why. Cite current file and line references. Do not edit.

results.text:
I recommend a `stream_to:` option on `tell_with_completion/5` as the first slice. The agent process relays each event to that recipient, rather than the prompt task sending it directly. I checked this against local `main` at `8f6cb9d` by reading the code only; I ran nothing and edited nothing except the plan file.

**The issue is partly out of date.** The prompt task already has the request ref: `dispatch/5` passes `{owner, request_ref}` into `run_prompt/7` (`lib/gen_agent/server.ex:1094-1103`, `1156-1164`), where it's used for checkpoints. It just isn't passed down to `consume_stream` or `maybe_handle_stream_event` (`server.ex:1180`, `1403`). The other claims still hold:
- `handle_stream_event/2` has no ref (`lib/gen_agent.ex:296`).
- The prompt-start telemetry event fires after the task is spawned (`server.ex:1109-1111`).
- Completion is a single message.
- There is no telemetry event per stream event.

**Why `stream_to` rather than the other two options:**
- **It needs no agent-module changes.** A LiveView passes `stream_to: self()` and matches on the ref it already has. A `handle_stream_event/3` callback would still make every module do its own forwarding, and it changes the callback contract.
- **The option list already exists.** `tell_with_completion/5` already takes and validates `on_halt:` (`gen_agent.ex:679-690`), so this is one more key.
- **Telemetry doesn't fit a per-request consumer.** Handlers run inside the prompt task, every handler sees every agent's events, and there's no recipient. It belongs in a later observability change.

**Why relay through the agent:** BEAM only orders messages between one sender and one receiver. With the relay, every event message from the task reaches the agent before the task's result does, and the agent forwards each one before sending the completion. So every delta is guaranteed to arrive before its completion message. On interrupt or watchdog, `current_request` is cleared (`server.ex:1709`, `1760`), so leftover event messages hit the existing catch-all at `server.ex:731` and are dropped. Nothing arrives after the completion. A direct send from the task can't promise that ordering.

**How the core change works:**
- **Message shape:** `{:gen_agent, :stream, name, ref, %Event{}}`. I used the `:stream` tag instead of the issue's `:event`, which would be confused with `notify/2` events.
- **Where the recipient is stored:** a separate `stream_recipients` map keyed by ref, rather than a change to the request `kind` tuples. Those tuples are pattern-matched in about 12 places.
- **Lifecycle:** the entry is removed at the top of `try_dispatch`, which covers pre_turn skip, halt and dispatch rejection. It is also removed on queued cancel and when a halt fails queued requests.
- **Compatibility:** when `stream_to` isn't given, the old call shape is sent unchanged, so Ensemble isn't affected.

**What the plan covers:**
- **Queued requests:** no stream messages until the request is dispatched.
- **Early deltas:** they can arrive before `{:ok, ref}` returns, as completions can today, and none are lost.
- **Cancellation and rejection:** a cancelled or rejected request gets zero stream messages and one completion.
- **Existing callbacks:** `handle_stream_event/2` still runs first, unchanged.
- **Dead recipients:** sends to a dead `stream_to` are dropped and the agent keeps running.
- **Backpressure:** there is none, and the docs should say so.

**Tests:** nine deterministic cases, reusing the gated backend in `test/gen_agent/request_completion_test.exs:6-30` with a lazy stream that waits between events. They use ref-matched `assert_receive`/`refute_receive` and no sleeps.

**Ensemble follow-up (separate PR):** pass `stream_to` through to sub-agents (`extensions/ensemble/lib/gen_agent_ensemble/server.ex:684`) and wrap events with the ensemble token. Later core work: the telemetry event, emitting prompt-start before spawning the task, and an optional `handle_stream_event/3`.

The full plan is in `/Users/joshrotenberg/.claude/plans/read-only-api-designer-verify-velvety-cloud.md`.
